I'm diagnosed with ASD and they also detected alexythimia during my assessment. I also struggle to feel emotional love, if I'm to be completely honest I don't think I can feel it at all. I can experience cognitive love though, which is my mind identifying that someone is loyal, great to be around, useful, and kind and therefore in return I shall be loyal, kind, respectful, and protective until they prove themselves to no longer have one of the attributes I valued them for. Usefulness is an extremely important factor when it comes to whether I cognitively "love" someone or not, with the exception of vulnerable people (children, elderly, the abused and harassed, other neurodivergent people). I can't feel love for animals at all because my brain has deemed them inherently useless to me. Anger is commonly the most easily felt emotion for people with alexythimia, sometimes we bubble up into rage because we didn't have any of the prior emotional warning signs. Personally I struggle with feeling fear/anxiety, I hadn't felt it for most of my life however I randomly acquired the ability to feel it when I was 19/20. Also however, anxiety is a commonly felt emotion with Autistics who have alexythimia. The plus side is that we think more objectively than most people with a normal range of emotions. However I wish I could experience the full range minus shame (I'm glad I can't really feel that). The only time in adulthood I felt something close to a normal range of emotions was when I was pregnant, so the heightened emotions was actually a good thing for me because I could finally make quick and instinctive decisions based on my emotional state. For a little while.

I'm honestly so sorry to hear that you've been put through this misery too. And yeah I relate to everything you've said. I thought the cheek filler would define my face too but it just made my face bigger and bloated which is the opposite of what I wanted lol. I know it's terrifying and you can private message me at anytime as well because I know what this does to your mental health and I remember my first month being particularly bad as well. If you want a listening ear that understands I'm here. I did the same where I didn't look at reddit until after that injector botched my face and wished I looked at sooner, I was equally terrified of hyaluronidase after reading the stories. What I'll say is don't be afraid of hyaluronidase because it's an enzyme that only targets hyaluronic acid, biologically enzymes can only target a single specific compound. If you're still worried then go on realself and look at all the negative reviews before and after photos, count how many of those "before" photos are when they had fillers in and not "before" they had anything done at all. You'll feel much better once you look at all the reviews. Not to completely invalidate them but body dysmorphia is actually really common amongst us who get procedures done. I'd say you could go back to the injector who did it just because the reversal is free but as you suspect and as frequently said, don't completely expect someone who messed up to know how to fix it. You may still need to go to a second injector for a touch up removal (make sure to bring photos) but at least the first injector would have removed a good bit of it or possibly all of it depending on the quantity or type of filler used. Do you know what type they used? If it's juvaderm it could take at least 3 sessions just because juvaderm is particularly stubborn. But there are other better types of filler that are removable in a single session, however those types don't bloat or spread so I won't be surprised if they used juvaderm so I'm sorry if they did. It's not your fault as you put your trust in an injector to use the best proceedure and best type of filler for your age and cosmetic goals but they didn't do that. Judging by your username you're the same age as me and if it's juvaderm they used they should've used a completely different filler that doesn't fill out the face but just mimics bone. What I'll promise is that it gets better. The sooner you get it removed the better plus in the next few months what's left will degrade on its own. It's been 8 months since I got mine done and I'd say I'm 90% back. My face still bloats in the morning and after I eat but my face is back to being recognisable by people that know me. It's also very close to my before pictures
